steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Take a count of the dead and wounded.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: It's just as you said. They used us as bait, and a battle ensued.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Are you disappointed, Talulah?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: —No.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: They had their reasons for doing this, and I also know exactly what they were. Knowing they had a legitimate reason, I couldn't possibly have gotten my hopes up.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: ...The informant must be executed.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: And how should we pick out this traitor, out of all the people that wanted to flee the battlefield?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: They betrayed their brothers-in-arms for a moment of peace. If you make excuses for them, you're only putting your warriors in harm's way.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: No. They never swore their loyalty to us in the first place.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You want every last person on your team to be absolutely perfect? That's impossible. You won't find a squad like that anywhere.

steps.name: Shieldguard
steps.text: But the guerrillas—

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The guerrilla fighters aren't perfect either.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: There are only a handful of people as perfect as you're making them out to be. Everyone else has their own reasons to be here, and only because they are willing to pay the price, but that doesn't mean they've thought it all through.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Stand down, soldier. Don't try to argue with her.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It takes a lot more work to build a city than to destroy one, Mister. Just let them stay.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If there's more than one way for the Infected to survive, I'd rather see all of those ways work out.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Talulah, you can't always try to go about everything without making sacrifices.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Sacrifices...

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Is that even up to me to decide?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: All of us are prepared for the worst. You can't win without spilling blood.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Heading south will lead to war. I know it, and I am sure you know it too.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: The Empire isn't going to sit by and watch the Infected unite and grow into a major force. If everything goes the way you pitched it and the Infected actually manage to take their fate into their own hands, then this war is inevitable.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: —You're right.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: We need to first let the Infected understand that their lives have meaning.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: They don't have an obligation to face anything that comes after that.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: You want the guerrillas to fight this war?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Talulah, are you waiting for a war to break out between Ursus and another country, one that you can profit from...?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Or are you trying to sow the seeds of that war yourself?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: (Silence)

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: You don't want to give me an answer.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: You should know that any victory you can hope to achieve will bring with it disastrous results.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You're probably right.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But that doesn't mean I'm going to sacrifice any lives.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Are you prepared to bear the tremendous pain to come?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Not at all. Things are bound to be painful, after all.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Do you expect everyone to be so kind-hearted?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I simply have faith that the people of Ursus weren't born selfish and cruel.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Perhaps you'll come face to face with real evil one day.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I've already crossed paths with my old friend a few times.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: I sure hope so.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If a soldier swears loyalty to his fellow men only to later betray them for his own profit, I will personally write up his charges.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: But if the group of Infected we are dealing with aren't fighting for the same cause as us, what gives us the right to annihilate them? It doesn't make them our enemies.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: Talulah!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Ngh...!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Please, go on.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: There are a lot of people whom I respected. Not for their strength, but for their honesty.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: —I can only hope you are one of them.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...I will keep that in mind.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Petrova, where's FrostNova at right now?

steps.name: Petrova
steps.text: ...She's still at the mountain pass. She said she's holding the fort there until we finish capturing the city.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Let's rendezvous with them. I need to apologize to her personally.

steps.name: Shieldguard
steps.text: So... Is that it, Captain?

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: There should still be at least three garrisons around. We need to take down every last one of them before we can get the supplies out.

steps.name: Patriot
steps.text: All things considered, she made the right decision. The nomadic city doesn't have that much longer of a walk ahead of it.

steps.name: Eno
steps.text: Oh, Talulah!

steps.name: Eno
steps.text: Are you in a bad mood, Talulah?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Nope, I'm fine.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: ...Eno, Sasha.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Do you still want me to use your real names?

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: ...Why do you ask?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It's better to have a name that we can use to protect ourselves when we are so far away from home.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Sometimes, if we don't pick a name for ourselves, we will only ever be called the names others give us.

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: But you haven't ever given yourself another name.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: That's only because I don't want to.

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: Why? You were just saying we should use different names.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Because... I want to be the same person both inside and out. I want to become someone whose actions represent her beliefs.

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: So then your current actions are different from your words.

steps.name: Eno
steps.text: Sasha!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You're right. That's very likely.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: That's why I insist on using my name. It's just that the name doesn't really have much meaning to everyone else.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: After all, who I am isn't important to any of them. My name is only important to myself.

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: So what should I call you, then? When you put it like this, I'm not sure what I'm supposed to call you.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Sasha, how about I put it this way, then?

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I'm just a rebel, just a normal person.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: My name? That's not important. No one should remember my name. This name shouldn't become a symbol, and it shouldn't come to have any other kind of power. It's just my name, and it's nothing more than a name.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: If you want to call me by a name, you can just call me Talulah for now. When you call me by my name, I'll turn around and look back, but that's all there is to it.

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: Talulah.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: You can call me Talulah too, Eno.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It may be a little too early to tell you two this... but I want to, Sasha.

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: Go on.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I want you call me Talulah because I want you to think of me as a friend. Good friends like we're all peas in a pod.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Even if I die, you will still remember my name, but not because I did anything special during my lifetime.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: I just want you to remember the time we spent together. I want you to remember you once had a friend called Talulah.

steps.name: Sasha
steps.text: But you're killing bad guys. You're fighting them.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The girl who fights shouldn't have a name. Everyone has their own fight. We are all fighters.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Don't hang your head and just follow in the fighters' footsteps. Don't do that!

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Not everyone is like Patriot. All of us make mistakes. Look ahead of you, and look at where he's going. You don't just keep your eyes shut and follow whoever that has the more important-sounding title.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: The names you remember are your friends' names. The names of the people you spend the most time with.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: It's FrostNova who gave you that extra spicy candy but still gritted her teeth and smiled. It's your teacher, who made you that weird vegetable stew. It's Patriot, who will never give up on training you.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: They are all your friends, not fighters.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: As fighters, we don't have names.

steps.name: Eno
steps.text: ...Talulah, I don't get it.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Well... I want you to trust me because I'm your friend, not because of my position.

steps.name: Talulah
steps.text: Just like all my other friends.
